h: How to win (or at least not come last)
p: Golf Fang is an 18+ venue, so think of it as a night out with a putter rather than a family day. Crazy golf rewards a gentle touch far more than brute force, so the person who smashes every shot usually ends up chasing the ball round the hole. Line up your putt, take a breath and let the slope do the work. It's surprising how often the self-confessed rubbish golfer comes out on top.

Keep the game moving with a bit of etiquette: one person on the tee at a time, no hovering over someone else's ball, and a scorekeeper who's trusted by everyone. If there's a big group of you, split into smaller teams and stagger your start so nobody's stood about waiting. Settle any forfeits before the first hole, not after the last.

Glasgow is a city built for a night out, and there's plenty to do the day before or after. The Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum is free to visit and packed with everything from Dalí to a Spitfire, and the Riverside Museum on the Clyde is brilliant for transport fans. Buchanan Street and the Merchant City are full of bars and restaurants, and the Glasgow Subway's little orange trains make zipping between the city centre and the West End easy. If you're making a weekend of it, a walk round Glasgow Green or up to the Necropolis gives you great views after a late night.
